subject: Novacorp operational charter & KPI handshake
body:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novacorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novacorp operational charter & KPI handshake

Elena — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick written recap from our discovery and the operational charter draft attached. This is intentionally pragmatic so we can converge on a measurable pilot. Please review and flag anything off the mark.

Top-line success criteria (pilot scope: retrieval-augmented generation on customer support workflow):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation <= 200 ms for < 512 token outputs under realistic client concurrency (measured with the same request patterns you shared).
- Throughput: sustained 40 requests/sec with burst capacity to 80 rps for short windows during load tests.
- Cost: average inference cost <= $0.0007 per token (model + infra blended) measured on pilot traces.
- Quality: QA pass on evaluation set: top-1 accuracy >= 92% for intent classification, mean embedding cosine >= 0.87 for retrieval ranking; spot-checks for hallucination rate < 2% on critical queries.

Pilot timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (Nov 2): onboarding sandbox, dataset ingest, and small-scale sanity runs.
- Weeks 1–3 (Nov 9–29): iterative tuning, instrumentation (latency/trace hooks), and runbook validation.
- Week 4 (Nov 30–Dec 6): scaled stress tests and acceptance measurement.
- Week 5 (Dec 7–Dec 13): review, handoff, and decision window.

Ownership (proposed):
- Redwood AE / primary contact: Rachel Kim — coordinate milestones, rollout decisions.
- Redwood Sales lead: Ben Carter — pricing, contracting, procurement liaison.
- Redwood Solutions / infra lead: Karthik Iyer — test harness, latency tuning, and ops runbook.
- Redwood CS: Priyom Das — success measurement and onboarding to production SLA if pilot passes.

Next practical steps (actionable):
1) Can you confirm acceptance criteria above (particularly latency and quality targets) or call out any changes by EOD Tue Nov 3?
2) If acceptable: we’ll schedule a 45-minute technical kickoff (Karthik + engineering on your side) the week of Nov 2 to validate test harness and data mapping.
3) I’ve attached an operational charter and an initial cost model from our side — Ben will follow up with a short pricing note and an SLA draft for the pilot.

Attachments: novacorp_pilot_operational_charter.pdf, redwood_poc_cost_model.xlsx

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0118

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novacorp.com>

Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novacorp operational charter & KPI handshake

Rachel — thanks for the recap and the clear breakdown. A couple of requests/clarifications from our side:
1) Latency: for the most critical agent path we were hoping to target p95 <= 150 ms (our SLAs with end customers are aggressive). Is that achievable with your recommended model/quantization profile?
2) Procurement: looping in procurement to begin standard info (SOC2, data residency, contract template).
3) Cost: can Ben give a ballpark cost range (pilot-only estimate) we can use for internal approvals this week — rough numbers are OK.
4) Evaluation set: we will send a 500-query sample (anonymized) by Monday for you to run a baseline.

I appreciate the timeline. Please add any security/compliance evidence we can share with procurement.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Integrations, Novacorp
elena.morales@novacorp.com | +1 617-555-0222

To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@novacorp.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Novacorp operational charter & KPI handshake

Quick technical notes on the latency ask and measurement method:
- 150 ms p95 is tight but not impossible for many of our optimized model variants if we cap context to 512 tokens and use continuous batching with a max batch window of 5 ms. We should test both the optimized Llama2-70b-int8 variant and a smaller 13b-int8 model as a fallback for stricter latency.
- Our p95 numbers are measured end-to-end (client -> redwood runtime -> model -> token stream completion). It’s important your client-side timeout and average request size match the pilot traces; divergence will change p95 significantly.
- Cost assumptions (attached spreadsheet): we modeled token mix (prompt vs. completion), batching efficiency, and GPU selection. Ballpark: pilot baseline ~$1,200–$1,800/week depending on traffic profile and model choice.

I’ll attach the cost workbook (redwood_poc_cost_model.xlsx) — we’ll iterate once we see your sample queries.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Pricing & pilot commercial note — Novacorp (NOVA-3421)

Elena / Procurement —
Following Rachel’s charter and Karthik’s cost workbook, quick commercial framing for internal approvals:
- Pilot term: 6-week pilot, pilots are charged at cost with a one-time setup fee. We typically provide a credit of up to $6,000 toward the pilot for verified production intent — happy to make that formal in the pilot SOW.
- Pricing range (pilot only, estimate): $7,500–$12,000 total for the pilot period depending on model selection and traffic patterns (this reflects the $1.2k–$1.8k/week that Karthik called out).
- If Novacorp converts to Dedicated / Reserved capacity within 90 days post-pilot, we’ll apply a 15% credit toward first-month committed spend.

Attached: redwood-pilot-sla-draft.docx

Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement to walk through terms — Rachel, can you propose 30–45 minute slots?

Best,
Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0333

Elena — thanks for the quick read.
- I’ll propose two kickoff slots for next week (Nov 2 or Nov 4) for the technical kickoff (Karthik + your engineers).
- Ben — appreciate the pilot commercial framing; procurement, Ben can set a short call to walk the SLA and credits.
- We’ll run the baseline against your 500-query anonymized sample and return per-criterion measurements within 48 hours of receiving it.

Please confirm sign-off on the acceptance criteria (latency p95: either 200 ms or, if you want to push, we’ll attempt 150 ms as a stretch target) by end of day Nov 3 so the team can lock the test matrix.

If there are security artifacts procurement needs (SOC2 report, data retention policy, export controls), I’ve asked our security team to prepare a short packet and Ben will drop a link into HubSpot for your procurement team.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Rachel
